summary: Pittsburgh Public Schools would face a significant increase in annual broadband costs if E-Rate ends, with an estimated $7.3 million increase over ten years.

claims.argument: Loss of E-Rate would increase annual broadband costs for Pittsburgh Public Schools by $7.3 million over ten years
claims.evidence_quote:
If E-Rate ends, PPS pays 100% of these costs instead of 10%:
•	Primary internet (Zito, 3-year, $81,000): we pay $8,100 today ($225/month). Without E-Rate: $81,000 ($2,250/month).
•	Wide area network (5-year, $2,250,000): we pay $225,000 today ($3,750/month). Without E-Rate: $2,250,000 ($37,500/month).
•	Recurring total: about $47,700/year today vs. $477,000/year without E-Rate, an increase of about $429,300 per year (10x).
•	Network upgrade (Fortinet, $5.9 million installed): E-Rate covered just over $3 million. Spread over a 7 to 10 year refresh cycle, that is roughly $300,000 to $430,000 per year the district would have to fund on its own.
•	Combined: roughly $730,000 to $860,000 more per year, or about $7.3 million over ten years.

filer_raw: Ira Weiss/Solicitor on behalf of Pittsburgh Public Schools
